two-vectors.t: Two vectors, **u and v**. We want a number that says **how much they point the same way**.

dot-product.t: Multiply matching entries and add: **u · v = u₁v₁ + u₂v₂**. The result is **one number**.

aligned.t: When v points the same way as u, the dot product is **large and positive**: the vectors share a lot of direction.

perpendicular.h: TURN v TO A RIGHT ANGLE
perpendicular.t: Rotate v until it makes a **right angle** with u. They no longer share any direction.

zero-dot.t: At **90°** the dot product is exactly **0**. Vectors with **u · v = 0** are called **orthogonal**.

ml-meaning.t: **Orthogonal directions are independent**: they do not overlap, so each coordinate can be read off separately. That is why machine learning likes them.
